title: Ambati Rayudu Says Hardik Pandya Felt Cornered as Mumbai Indians Captain
excerpt: The former CSK batter told Cricbuzz Pandya should give up the MI captaincy if he stays — and avoid KKR — as reports link him with a player-only move to Punjab Kings.
body:
• Former CSK batter Ambati Rayudu said on Cricbuzz that Hardik Pandya "felt as if he was cornered" during his Mumbai Indians captaincy.
  • Rayudu advised Pandya to give up the MI captaincy if he stays in IPL 2027, and to play as a match-winner without the leadership burden.
  • Rayudu named Punjab Kings and CSK as better fits than KKR, which he said would expect Pandya to captain an inexperienced side.
  • Separately, PTI reported via Circle of Cricket that MI and Punjab Kings are in advanced talks on a Pandya–Arshdeep Singh swap in which Pandya would join Punjab as a player only.

Ambati Rayudu has offered the bluntest public assessment yet of Hardik Pandya's Mumbai Indians captaincy, saying the all-rounder looked like a man watching his back in his own dressing room. Speaking during a discussion on Cricbuzz amid the trade rumours surrounding Pandya, the former India and Chennai Super Kings batter said Pandya should not captain Mumbai Indians again if he stays with the franchise for IPL 2027, according to Sportskeeda's report of the discussion. NDTV Sports carried the same comments.

"In Mumbai, I just thought that Hardik felt as if he was cornered. And once you feel you're cornered, you're always looking over your shoulder."

— Ambati Rayudu, on Cricbuzz

Rayudu added that once that feeling sets in inside a dressing room, a player "tends to just come out in ways that you wouldn't want to," and that a lot of things did not go well for Hardik — some of it, he conceded, possibly Pandya's own fault as well.

"Just Play His Game"

His prescription was specific. "From now on, if he wants to stay at MI, I don't think he should be the captain. He should just play his game, enjoy his time, and be a match-winner for MI. But if he goes out, definitely not a captain again, at least for one season," Rayudu said.

https://x.com/gullypoint_/status/2118188733350748617

The contrast with Pandya's earlier captaincy record is the context Rayudu was speaking into. Pandya led Gujarat Titans to the title in their debut season in 2022 and to a runners-up finish the following year. At Mumbai, where he returned ahead of the 2024 season and was appointed captain, the side has qualified for the playoffs just once in three years under his leadership. Pandya has also been on the sidelines since May 2026 with injuries and is undergoing rehabilitation at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.

KKR a No, Punjab or CSK a Yes

Rayudu also steered Pandya away from Kolkata Knight Riders, another franchise linked with him ahead of IPL 2027. KKR, he argued, would look at Pandya as a captaincy candidate, and leading that inexperienced side would be a heavy load. "I think either Punjab or CSK because these are the two teams he'll go but he'll not captain, and he'll find a very, very good space in terms of his cricket. But with KKR, there's so much on the plate that he needs to assess and take things forward because they need a captain. It's not an easy team to captain right now," he said.

The Punjab Talks Point the Same Way

Rayudu's preferred destination aligns with the strongest reported move. Circle of Cricket, citing PTI, reported that Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings are in advanced negotiations over a swap that would send Pandya to Punjab and Arshdeep Singh plus another player to Mumbai, with the senior managements having agreed in principle. An IPL source told PTI the talks are ongoing but "not a done deal yet." Crucially for Rayudu's argument, Punjab — captained by Shreyas Iyer, who led the franchise to the 2025 final — has conveyed that Pandya would join purely as a player, with the Ricky Ponting-coached side targeting his all-round skills to reinforce a bowling attack that struggled in the second half of the 2026 season.

The same reporting says Rohit Sharma is widely expected to regain the Mumbai Indians captaincy for 2027 if Pandya leaves. Franchises have until the extended retention deadline of November 17 to finalise their lists, ahead of the mini-auction in Goa on December 16 — so whether Pandya stays and sheds the captaincy, as Rayudu advises, or leaves without it, the answer arrives within days.
